aliases.name: M16A2
aliases.note: The 1983 variant this entry’s dimensions describe.

capacity.sourceNote: STANAG magazines of 20, 30, 40 and 60 rounds and a 100-round drum are listed.

variants.name: M16A1
variants.summary: Forward assist, chrome-lined chamber and a 1:12 twist. The rifle of the Vietnam War, and the one whose early reliability problems produced a Congressional inquiry.

variants.name: M16A2
variants.summary: Three-round burst instead of automatic, a heavier barrel in 1:7 twist for the new SS109 bullet, and an adjustable rear sight. The configuration this entry’s dimensions describe.

variants.name: M16A4
variants.summary: A flat-top receiver with a Picatinny rail in place of the fixed carrying handle.

images.alt: Two views of an M16A2 rifle isolated on white, left and right sides, showing the carrying handle, the ribbed round handguard and a curved magazine
images.caption: An M16A2 from the Swedish Army Museum — the configuration this entry’s weight, length and barrel figures describe.

massEmpty.sourceNote: Published as 7.5 lb; 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg exactly. M16A2, without magazine or sling.

length.sourceNote: Published as 39.63 in; 1 in = 25.4 mm exactly. M16A2.

barrelLength.sourceNote: Published as 20 in; 1 in = 25.4 mm exactly.

cyclicRate.sourceNote: The article publishes 700–900 rounds/min for the M16A2 and M16A3 and a single 800 for the M16A4. Recorded as the M16A4 figure, which falls inside the earlier range.

effectiveRange.sourceNote: Published as the point-target effective range; 800 m is given for an area target.

productionTotal.sourceNote: The cited article gives "~8 million" for the M16 itself, separately from about 28 million AR-15–style rifles.
